query: Help me understand what's in these airline reviews — I'm not sure which aspect is most worth analyzing.

per_column.name: dominant_topic
per_column.rationale: Directly serves the exploratory query by giving an aspect-level grouping axis over free-text reviews, letting the analyst see which themes dominate. Categories are well-diversified and non-constant. Groundedness is mostly sound: seat_comfort, food, and staff samples map cleanly to their text. One sample (row 4) is dominated by extensive food description yet labeled 'staff', a defensible but weaker reading, and row 1 mentions many topics with 'staff' being reasonable. Minor mislabeling lowers groundedness slightly but no invented facts.

per_column.name: review_sentiment
per_column.rationale: A bare positive/negative/neutral sentiment flag is fairly generic and partly redundant with existing 'Overall Rating', 'Value For Money', and 'Recommended' columns, limiting new analytical leverage. However for an open-ended 'what's in these reviews' exploration it still offers a text-derived axis crossable with dominant_topic. Values are well-grounded in the sampled source text (positives correctly identified, negative seat review correctly negative).

per_column.name: review_length_category
per_column.rationale: Bucketed text length is a generic metadata feature that adds little analytical leverage for understanding review CONTENT; it is close to the 'raw text length' case flagged as low value. Values are broadly derivable from the text but the thresholds appear inconsistent: the row-3 review is comparably short yet the row-1 review, similar in length, is 'medium' while a clearly longer row-4 review is 'long' — buckets are plausible but somewhat arbitrary.

judge.rationale: The set centers on one genuinely valuable column (dominant_topic) that gives real aspect-level grouping for an exploratory query, supported by a moderately useful sentiment axis. review_length_category drags usefulness down as generic metadata. Groundedness is strong overall: values are sound readings of source text with no invented facts, only a couple of debatable topic assignments and arbitrary length thresholds. Judged only on usefulness and groundedness, not completeness.
